studies.label: Classroom factorial RCT: causal-reasoning training and ChatGPT Edu access
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Intact classes were randomized within degree program. PDF p. 17 (printed p. 16), Appendix Section 1, reports 13 classes and one class per program per arm, except two Management classes in Causal&GPT. Per-arm class totals are not separately printed and remain null under the transcription-only rule. SEs use cells formed from mother tongue, high-school type and class (PDF p. 37, printed p. 36, Appendix Section 4); Tables A.12-A.14 explicitly report 50 clusters (PDF pp. 46-48, printed pp. 45-47). These cells subdivide the randomized classes. The reported regressions have one observation per participant, but do not report precision clustered by the randomized class. se_basis is participant, not cluster; these SEs do not qualify for pooling in this class-randomized study.

open_items: Observed arm means, arm-level outcome SDs and arm-level diversity uncertainty are not printed. Table A.7 contains full-sample summaries only; regression constants are not substituted for arm levels.

Assignment-class clustered SEs are unavailable. The reported intersection-cell clustering subdivides randomized classes. se_basis=participant describes one analyzed score per student; it does not make these SEs eligible for pooling when assignment_unit=class. Re-estimation using the randomized classes is needed.

Numerical per-arm class totals are not explicitly tabulated. The allocation rule is recorded in cluster_se_treatment; clusters_per_arm remains null under the instruction not to calculate unprinted numbers.

The named-arm combined participant totals are not printed; n_total is null rather than calculated or replaced with the all-arm regression count. Full regression counts are recorded in regression.model with an Observations-row source.

The two single-idea responses missing within-solution diversity are not assigned to arms in the report. Their omission also affects the PDS specifications that include diversity controls; analyzed arm counts for those models remain null.
Causal&GPT versus Causal and Causal&GPT versus GPT estimates and their SEs/tests are not printed directly; component coefficients and SEs do not supply the covariance needed for these contrasts.

The between-solution diversity outcome uses the pooled sample as a reference. Arm-specific output-pool similarity/diversity and exact averaging weights over other responses and their ideas are not reported.
The preregistration identifier and original plan are unavailable, so preregistered outcome priority cannot be verified.
The participant country and the release year of the assigned GPT-4o/ChatGPT Edu tool are not explicitly stated in the paper and remain null.
Main-text case duration and appendix session duration are not consistently distinguished; no task-only duration is inferred.
No shared-participant relationship with another paper is reported in the screening form or paper; this is not proof that no overlap exists.
notes: Reconciliation checked the entire markdown conversion, including all appendix sections and references, then checked cited PDF pages with PyMuPDF text extraction. find_tables detected no tables on the numeric result pages; their extracted text preserves the printed rows and column order. All reported coefficients, SEs, significance bounds and counts were checked independently. A and B contain the same 26 model specifications after matching by outcome, expert reference, table and column; the supplied diff cross-matched several distinct specifications. All unique diff field disagreements are resolved; repeated identical count entries in that diff share one resolution. only_in_a and only_in_b are empty, and no additional eligible numerical result was found. A slugs are used for the final records. Agreed fields were independently audited: usefulness for expert-scored marketing effectiveness; fluency for core-idea counts; flexibility for distances within one response; across_people/diversity only for the pooled-reference between-student measure; with_ai/other for expert alignment and output-scored reasoning attributes. Each analysis uses one participant-level outcome; neither the raters, repeated LLM scores nor underlying idea comparisons are independent participant counts. higher_is describes the literal scale direction. All scored recommendations were produced with AI available in the AI arms; the design is between subjects. n_total remains null because named-pair totals are not printed. Arm counts are retained only for complete-sample models; the affected arms in reduced models are unknown. No number is calculated from coefficients, regression constants, SDs, counts or figure coordinates. Raw-table precision and signs are preserved in source quotes; the coherent-logic paper_effect is the approximate standardized value explicitly printed in prose. Full-sample descriptive SDs are not arm SDs and are not substituted as standardizers. Alternative OLS/PDS specifications share participants; PDS models condition on post-treatment output features and are not the baseline total treatment effect. se_basis was corrected in every record: the paper uses participant-level observations with clustering cells inside randomized classes, not randomized-class precision. Those SEs are retained for reporting and are unsuitable for pooling under the class-randomization requirement. All screening outcomes and contrasts are represented or explicitly listed in not_extracted. No effect, SE, interval, mean, SD, coefficient sum or participant total was derived.
